title: Reveal Cards In Increasing Order
statement:
You hold the cards `deck`, each showing a different integer, and may stack them face down in any order you choose. Then this ritual repeats until no card is left: turn over the top card and set it aside; then, if any cards remain in the stack, take the new top card and slide it underneath to the bottom.

Return an ordering of the cards (index `0` is the top of the stack) for which the cards are turned over in increasing order of their values.
constraints: All values in deck are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

The ritual never looks at the values: which position of the stack is turned over first, second, third... depends only on how many cards there are. So run the ritual on the positions `0..n-1` instead of on cards. A queue of positions plays the stack: the front position is revealed, the next one goes to the back. The `k`-th position revealed must hold the `k`-th smallest card.

Trying all orderings and simulating each would cost O(n! · n); the simulation on positions costs only O(n) after sorting.

## Approach

1. Sort the cards ascending into `sorted`.
2. Put every position `0..n-1` into `queue`, with `head` marking its front.
3. For each `card` in increasing order: take the front position `slot` and write `card` into `result[slot]`.
4. If positions remain, move the next front position to the back of `queue`, just as the ritual moves a card to the bottom.
5. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`sorted = [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17]`, `queue = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]`.

- `2` goes to slot `0`; `1` moves back, the queue is `[2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 1]`.
- `3` goes to slot `2`; `3` moves back: `[4, 5, 6, 1, 3]`.
- `5` goes to slot `4`: `[6, 1, 3, 5]`. `7` goes to slot `6`: `[3, 5, 1]`.
- `11` goes to slot `3`: `[1, 5]`. `13` goes to slot `1`: `[5]`. `17` goes to slot `5`.
- `result = [2, 13, 3, 11, 5, 17, 7]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): the sort dominates; the simulation makes at most `2n` queue steps.
- Space: O(n) for the sorted copy, the queue and the result.

## Pitfalls

- Simulate positions, not values: the queue holds indices of `result`, and cards are written into them.
- Skip the move to the bottom after the last reveal; with nothing left there is no card to move.
- `Array.prototype.shift` is O(n) per call; a `head` pointer keeps each queue step O(1).
- Sort numerically with `(a, b) => a - b`; the default sort compares digits as text.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sorted` | the cards in increasing order, the order they must be revealed |
| `result` | the stack ordering being filled in |
| `queue` | stack positions in the order the ritual will visit them |
| `head` | index of the front of `queue` |
| `card` | the next card to be revealed |
| `slot` | the position that is revealed now, which receives `card` |

narration.2: Sort a copy of the cards: they must come out in this order.
narration.3: The answer array, filled position by position.
narration.4: A queue of stack positions stands in for the stack itself.
narration.5: Initially the positions are in stack order, top first.
narration.8: head marks the front of the queue, so no element is shifted.
narration.10: Hand out the cards from smallest to largest.
narration.11: The position at the front is the one revealed next...
narration.13: So the smallest card not yet placed belongs there.
narration.14: If positions remain, the ritual moves the next top card to the bottom.
narration.15: Send the next front position to the back of the queue.
narration.16: It is no longer at the front.
narration.19: Every position has received its card; return the ordering.
